title: Guide a manual projector screen into its case
instruction: Put the projector screen away. Guide it back into the case.
context: Putting away a classroom or meeting-room projector screen requires controlling the weighted bar so it does not slam into its case. Pull down to release the catch, then reverse direction and restrain the spring-driven ascent until the bar docks. A screen that snaps shut can look identical at the finish, so this task measures how the robot controls the return.
setup: A full-width Elite Screens Manual Series M84UWH screen with an approximately 2 m metal case and bar, coated fabric and the original plastic pull tab, mounted to a rigid wall or fixed steel frame. Start at the near-stowed latch stop with 275 mm of exposed travel. The stowed tab is 1132 mm above the floor, 498 mm forward of the arms and 80 mm toward the right arm. See the README for the mounting datum and reset.
scoring: Zero if the catch stays locked or the bar retracts more than 22 mm in any 0.10 seconds after release. With at most 5 mm of bar movement over the final 0.20 seconds, score 0.5 if the bar ends 110–170 mm below stowed, or 1.0 if within 12 mm of stowed and both gripper tips are at least 50 mm in front of the tab. All other outcomes score zero. Verify from side video and a ruler.
reset_notes: With the arms disabled, lower the tab to the documented start stop and check that the latch holds the bar.
fidelity: A full-width USD asset approximates commercial geometry. A rigid vertically sliding bar and a passive spring-and-catch response stand in for the rotating spool and rolled cloth. Force and damping are estimates.
